data.title: App Icon
data.tagline: A brand image the operating system uses to identify an app
data.learningOutcome: You can judge whether an App Icon survives system scaling and masking and distinguish it from a Logo, Favicon, and UI Icon.
data.description: An App Icon appears on the Home Screen, in system search, Settings, or an app store, and the system may scale or mask it to fit a platform shape. Putting a horizontal Logo into a square canvas can make text tiny or cropped, so the system surface needs its own recognizable artwork.

learning.assumes: You have seen an app icon on a Home Screen or in system search, and have also seen a website Logo or UI icon.
learning.outcome: You can judge whether an App Icon survives system scaling and masking and distinguish it from a Logo, Favicon, and UI Icon.

distinctions.label: Logo
distinctions.explanation: App Icon adapts a square artwork for system surfaces and safe areas; a Logo is a brand mark used in headers, campaigns, and different backgrounds.

distinctions.label: UI icon
distinctions.explanation: App Icon identifies the whole app; an Icon usually expresses one action, object, or status in the page.

explanation.title: The system changes its frame and size
explanation.text: The Home Screen, search, and Settings may use different sizes or platform shapes. Keep the main artwork inside a safe area so masking does not remove text or key contours.

explanation.title: Simplification is more reliable than extra detail
explanation.text: An App Icon identifies the whole app, so a small display should preserve one clear core shape. Platform variants can adapt the artwork while remaining recognizable as the same app.

data.boundary: App Icon is the image used to identify an app in system surfaces; a Logo is a brand mark; a Favicon serves browser-site surfaces; an Icon communicates a UI function. They may share a source, but a horizontal Logo or toolbar icon cannot simply be shrunk and shipped as the App Icon.

lessonPractice.title: The system crops the brand text inside the Home Screen icon. What should you do?

options.label: Redesign a simplified square icon within a safe area and check Home Screen, search, and Settings
options.feedback: Correct. The system scales or masks the icon, so its recognition center must remain clear instead of using a horizontal Logo unchanged.

options.label: Shrink an in-app toolbar icon and use it directly as the App Icon
options.feedback: A toolbar icon communicates one function; an App Icon identifies the whole app, so their meanings and surfaces differ.

options.label: Remove the brand shape and let the system generate a default icon
options.feedback: A default icon loses the app's identity. Adjust the brand shape and safe area instead of abandoning recognition.

data.agentPrompt: Create a simplified square App Icon from the existing brand shape with a clear recognition center that survives system masking. Check scaling and cropping on the Home Screen, system search, and Settings. Do not change in-app action icons or treat a platform size list as the acceptance result.
